content.v: 日前，韩国游戏公司Joycity表示，旗下子公司 Wre 正在开发的新作足球游戏《自由足球2》（Freestyle Football 2）已开启预售，并将于12月3日全球正式上线。
《自由足球2》是一款强调快节奏攻防、个性鲜明角色、直观操作以及5v5团队合作乐趣的在线足球游戏。游戏中每个角色都有独特的定位和技能，以按位置协作的玩法为特点，并支持PC与主机平台之间的跨平台游玩，玩家可与不同平台用户同场竞技。
此次预售在正式上线前进行，活动期间购买游戏的所有用户可享受全版本10%的基础折扣。此外，Xbox Game Pass 和 PlayStation Plus 订阅用户还可在基础折扣上再享10%额外折扣，以优惠价格购买《自由足球2》。
《自由足球2》曾参加 Gamescom、PAX West、Steam Next Fest 等主要活动，扩大与全球玩家的接触点，加快上市准备。Joycity 计划在正式上线前推出预售纪念活动与促销，持续吸引全球玩家关注。
《自由足球2》将通过 Xbox Series X|S、Xbox on PC、PS5、PC Steam 在全球提供服务。

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20261015/rJrEeMbueEhfncu.jpg!a-3-480x.jpg
在 2025 年游戏大奖（Game Awards）上，演员、喜剧演员兼播客主持人 Andrew Schulz 在宣传他主演的 街头霸王6 电影（他在片中饰演火引弹）时，公开调侃了第二部 真人快打11 电影的演员阵容，此事引发了不小的争议。
街头霸王6
单人, 线上玩家对战, 同屏/分屏玩家对战, 跨平台联机游戏, Steam 成就, 完全支持控制器, 应用内购买, steam云, 动作, 冒险, 2D格斗, 街机, 格斗, 动作角色扮演, 角色自定义, 沙盒, 多人, 竞技, 开放世界
环球游历对于老玩家就是图一乐儿，“现代模式”对于新玩家绝非图一乐儿。
查看更多 立即下载
“我们不是唯一感谢各位支持的游戏，”Schulz 说道。“还有另一款游戏。他们也从世界各地飞来这里，因为他们感激你们。所以，让我们为 真人快打11 2 的全体演员鼓掌！”
真人快打11
暴力, 血腥, 动作, 格斗
查看更多 立即下载
事实证明，该片的演员们实际上并没有出现在游戏大奖现场，Schulz 借此在舞台上大做文章。“开个玩笑，”他继续说道。“他们没来。他们根本不在乎你们，他们只在乎钱，好吗？而我们既在乎钱也在乎你们！街头霸王6 万岁！”
街头霸王6 电影的演员阵容在游戏大奖上对 真人快打11 电影的演员们放了狠话！火药味十足！😤
尽管他的同剧组演员澄清这只是个玩笑，但 Schulz 的言论迅速走红，许多粉丝认为这是对同类格斗游戏改编作品的恶意攻击。甚至出演了该系列电影的演员 Lewis Tan 也对此事发表了看法，称 Schulz 是“最没资格在那个舞台上胡言乱语的人”。
在 街头霸王6 电影上映前，我有机会就这个笑话询问了 Schulz —— 他告诉我说，他只是想以经典的职业摔角方式，与 真人快打11 II 的演员们建立一种友好的竞争关系。
“伙计们，我以为我们是一伙的！在摔角界，这被称为‘演出（work）’，对吧？”Schulz 开始说道。
“没错。你是在演戏，而他们却当真了，”Cody Rhodes 证实道。
“我读的是提词器上的内容，”Schulz 继续说道。“……我以为我们会变成‘芭本海默’那样的联动。你知道的，水涨船高。”
“但你确实怼了他们，”Eric Andre 插话道。
“我帮他们赚足了热度，”Schulz 反驳道。
“我有个后续问题，”Rhodes 看着我问道。“你有 真人快打11 的纹身吗？”
（我觉得有必要解释一下；你可能看过这段采访的走红片段，这三个人在采访中让我展示 M. Bison 的纹身。）
“我没有，”我回答道。
“正是如此，”Schulz 说道，而 Cody 则回应称他并不是“想再次开火”。
“我还在等一句谢谢呢！”当我询问 Schulz 对其言论在网上引发的辩论有何看法时，他开玩笑地说道。“你看，我们利用自己的平台宣传我们的电影，同时也宣传了另一部电影！我觉得这是一件非常慷慨的事情！”
既然聊到了 真人快打11，我不得不提到该系列的联合主创 Ed Boon 最近表达了对与 街头霸王6 进行潜在交叉联动的兴趣。当被问及是否愿意出演一部跨界电影时，Schulz 告诉我，这本质上就是他在游戏大奖上那段走红言论想要达到的目的。
“这就是我们在游戏大奖上想要做的！”Schulz 说道。“我们正试图促成这件事！”
“那正是我们努力的方向，”Cody Rhodes 补充道。
“告诉他们我知道 Noob Saibot 是 [Ed Boon 和 John Tobias] 名字的倒写，”Eric Andre 插话道。“……但是联动？像《摩登原始人》和《杰森一家》那样的联动？我们加入。来吧。”
（三位演员都澄清说，他们对 真人快打11 系列及其电影演员充满敬意；这三位风趣的演员只是在和我调侃当时的情况，但显然他们非常愿意以某种形式与 真人快打11 的团队合作。）
我采访的大多数 街头霸王6 演员都表达了类似的观点。几乎每个人都愿意与其他格斗游戏系列合作，Andrew Koji 和 Callina Liang 特别提到了 Marvel vs Capcom。
然而，导演 Kitao Sakurai 明确表示，未来任何 街头霸王6 电影的计划都取决于第一部在影院的表现。就我个人而言，这部电影非常有趣，充满了粉丝们会喜欢的背景设定和彩蛋——但你需要在观看时形成自己的评价。
街头霸王6 将于 2026 年 10 月 16 日上映。

https://image.gcores.com/62fc0d07db2c9eee06a622969ad53112-1920-1080.jpg
剧情方面，光明骑士团实现了古老的预言，击败了毁灭一切生灵的恶人，为诸世界带来了希望。只剩下一件小事：把这里收拾干净，好让世界重新住上人。骑士团自己走进传送门去庆功了，临走前送了她一把拖把。拖把被她扔了。
https://image.gcores.com/5499c756eaf833c3f18a347b1f7c0bcf-1920-1080.jpg
在 PvP 方面下，周围的一切都能被拆掉，魔法也永远用不完。摧毁对手的掩体，把他脚下的地板轰塌，趁墙还没塌完赶紧躲在后面。每一回合都会换一种新法术，所以战术必须随时调整。

content.v: 《拉力赛艺术 art of rally》开发团队Funselektor宣布，全新越野探索游戏《越过山丘 over the hill》现已正式登陆Steam！游戏国区售价86元，发售前两周享八折首发优惠；配合捆绑包折扣叠加，游戏入手价可低至62元。
https://image.gcores.com/6ae67f281f75955338b4c4ebb47f4da4-1385-779.jpeg
《越过山丘 over the hill》支持1–4人游玩。玩家可以驾驶以20世纪60至80年代经典越野车型为灵感打造的座驾，独自或与最多三名好友一同驶入荒野。游戏世界以现实中的自然风光为灵感，玩家可以穿越森林、湖畔与山地，在广阔的自然环境中自由探索，挑战复杂地形，寻找属于自己的前进路线。
Funselektor创始人兼创意总监Dune Casu表示：
“我们真的很希望大家会喜欢《越过山丘》。说实话，直到现在，我们自己都有点不敢相信，它真的发售了。
在最开始，我们只是想做一款简单的探索游戏：开上一辆老式四驱越野车，驶进荒野，漫无目的，看看自己最终会开到哪里。
https://image.gcores.com/8f17bd9c800d43397dad00cfc5e989c9-1385-779.jpeg
过去十年里，我大多住在露营车里，一边生活、一边工作。我很喜欢开到一个偏远的地方，安静地待上一阵子，然后没有什么计划地再次出发，看看下一段路会把我带到哪个目的地。
这种感觉，可以说是《越过山丘》最重要的一部分。你可以按自己的节奏前进，一路走走停停，迷路也没关系。我们希望大家在玩的时候，能体味到独自上路时孤独感的美丽，也能在这段旅途中留下属于与朋友一起越野的美好回忆。”
https://image.gcores.com/3333b8efaa4c14eba92942d993f6bd86-1384-778.png
此外，想要进一步支持Funselektor的玩家，还可以购买《越过山丘 over the hill》支持者捆绑包。该捆绑包包含游戏本体、官方原声带和支持者礼包，国区售价为126元，发售前两周折后价约为113元。
支持者礼包包含：
《越过山丘 over the hill》游戏本体
专属车辆外观装饰，包括备胎、车牌和支持者名牌等
收录40首曲目的官方数字原声带
一个特别的露营地点，配有专属装饰、帐篷与篝火
官方数字原声带也可单独购买，售价为33元。
原声带共收录40首原创音乐，分为4张专辑，涵盖民谣、盯鞋摇滚、氛围电子等多种音乐风格，由Tatreal（Slava Korystov）与Giacomo Giunchedi创作并制作。
游戏现已登陆PC；PlayStation 5、Xbox Series X|S 和 Nintendo Switch 2版本计划于2027年推出。
核心特色
驶向人迹罕至之地
独自出发，或与最多三名好友结伴同行。沿着风景各异的路线深入荒野，挑战复杂地形，并利用木板、绞盘等装备共同跨越障碍。你可以提前规划路线，也可以根据现场情况灵活应对。
探索值得停留的世界
穿行于森林、湖畔与群山之间，寻找隐秘小屋、观景点、自然地标、陨石，以及通往新区域的传送门。动态天气与昼夜循环将持续影响沿途环境，为每一次探索带来不同的景观变化与行程体验。
记录旅途中的风景
寻找栖息于各地的野生动物，并用游戏内相机完善图鉴。你也可以随时停下脚步，拍下沿途风景，记录旅途中值得纪念的瞬间。
打造属于你的座驾
在探索过程中寻找升级部件与实用装备，并在商人或小屋处调整车辆。通过车身颜色、配件和外观装饰，打造一辆符合个人驾驶风格的越野车。
旅程本身就是答案
不必急着抵达终点。放慢速度，选择自己的路线，享受沿途发生的一切。毕竟，最值得讲述的故事，从来都不始于终点。

items.title: 推出三个月后，Riot 宣布英雄联盟经典版将于一月被取消：“大多数人已经回到了联盟的其他部分”
items.summary: New Champions will continue to roll out for now.

content.v: League of Legends Classic was Riot's attempt to capitalise on nostalgia for vintage-era LoL. It stripped away most of the champions and kits introduced since 2013, reverted to an older version of the Summoner's Rift map, and promised to roll out "new" old Champions at a faster clip than in the olden days.
But the nostalgia Riot must have hoped would sustain the mode hasn't proven sufficient enough to keep it running: the mode will go offline in January 2027, only six months after its launch.
"We’ve seen a lot of players have fun revisiting the olden days with Classic," a Riot spokesperson wrote in a new update . "At this point though, most have gone back to other parts of League."
As a result, the current season will be the last. "We’ll then put Classic back in the box for now, with the goal of bringing it back, likely as an event mode with adjustments and additions."

It continues: "There’s more we’re going to share in the future about what we learned from this run. That includes where we think we got Classic right, where we could have gone more classic, and where sticking too closely to the past may have held the experience back."

Refunds will be issued for Classic content rendered obsolete by the closure. And it's not the end of the line yet: there are at least seven more Champions still to roll out, including Mordekaiser, Yorick, Hecarim and Lucian in the forthcoming 26.21 update, and Vilibear, Urgot and Udyr in future ones.

"This game mode was a true labor of love from so many Rioters, and seeing you all dive back in to reclaim the nostalgia, reconnect with old friends, and relive your glory days made it a truly special moment for everyone. We will keep exploring different ways to play League and as always, we appreciate all of your feedback. Every post on social media asking for Classic, every vote cast in the Council, and every minute spent leashing for your jungler again helped us bring this to life, so thank you very much."

What was wrong with Classic? Back in August, League of Legends esports veteran Alex Chu (also known as Xpecial) offered his thoughts on why uptake might be slow for players accustomed to modern LoL. His words came at a time when a lot of the LoL community were criticising the concept.
Chu then speculated a future for Classic that never eventuated, or at least, likely won't now.

"The interesting part is what happens now that the reins are loosened," he added. "We could end up with a version of League that players vote for things that would never fly with a mass audience. More complicated drafts. The ability to ban a champion for an entire season. Forcing a marksman mid meta or a mage bot meta just because the council wants to see it. Modern League can't do any of that, because modern League has to appeal to everyone. Classic only has to appeal to enough people."

Chu's thoughts aside, it's possible that old LoL just doesn't have the nostalgic appeal of old World of Warcraft, old Runescape, or old Guild Wars. Those are spaces you inhabit and they are generally less high pressure and adversarial. They become a kind of home away from home, whereas LoL is always just a hugely competitive MOBA. A good one that you can build a lifestyle around, but a MMORPG it ain't.

LoL also evolves much faster than those older MMOs did. Back in 2013, LoL was receiving new champions every two to three weeks, which could affect the whole experience. By contrast, MMOs at the time generally only received seismic updates on a yearly basis at most: much more time for a game condition to sink in.

content.v: 随着《 战地6 》第5赛季上线，玩家迎来了新地图、武器等内容，DICE还悄悄加入了一些彩蛋。DICE把这个彩蛋放在了51区地图上。正如你可能猜到的，它与外星人有关。
我们不必再猜：一些富有想象力的玩家已经破解了彩蛋。找到它还能获得游戏内奖励。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261015/1792021216_328180.jpg
油管用户DANNYonPC上传了一段约四分钟的51区UFO彩蛋教程。
如果你更喜欢看文字，以下是《战地》彩蛋社群成员提供的分步指南：
高塔旁的箱子后面藏着按钮，需要用刀。
每座高塔都有编号（见地图）。
先查看各座高塔灯光的初始状态。
按正确顺序按下按钮，门就会打开，露出一间控制室。
右前方有一个启动按钮，按下后可以打开屏幕。
摩尔斯电码译为“INT RDRSUNDRGRND”（如图所示;这串文字可能使用了缩写，也可能尚未辨认清楚）。
大屏幕会显示一串符号，每次显示的内容都相同。
使用解谜工具找出正确顺序，让所有灯都变成绿色。
八盏灯全部变绿后，前往F目标附近隧道中的那扇锁着的门。
如果所有灯的状态都正确，密码键盘应该会变成绿色。与它互动即可开门。
进入控制室，与房间前方的无线电互动，打开屏幕。
显示器上的符号对应着八次按下按钮的顺序。
令人惊讶的是，这个彩蛋只用一天就被破解了！希望DICE在第5赛季还藏了更多秘密，让游戏更有趣。
虽然这个彩蛋和对应的武器挂饰奖励确实不错，但有证据显示，《战地6》第5赛季战斗通行证中的装饰物由AI制作，生成质量也不尽如人意，多少让人有些扫兴。

content.v: 汤姆·克鲁斯最近的票房表现不太理想。他备受期待的新片《Digger》原本有望为他的职业生涯开启新阶段，却远未成为票房大片。影片不仅引发了不少争议，票房也持续低迷，创下克鲁斯近20年来最低的首映票房。与此同时，他一部常被低估的电影却成了流媒体热门影片。如果你想看，得抓紧时间。
谈起汤姆·克鲁斯最好的电影，人们通常不会首先想到《世界大战》。这部2005年上映的科幻动作惊悚片改编自H.G.威尔斯1898年的小说，讲述一位蓝领父亲在外星人入侵地球后保护孩子，并设法让他们与母亲团聚的故事。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261015/1792020304_255929_jpg_r.jpg
影片由史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格执导，达科塔·范宁、米兰达·奥图和蒂姆·罗宾斯与克鲁斯共同出演，摩根·弗里曼担任旁白。影片票房表现不错，也获得影评人称赞，但当时的影迷并不买账。此后多年，影迷逐渐改变了看法。《世界大战》近期在多个国家跻身流媒体播放量前十。
不过，如果你想亲自看看，得尽快了：影片将于11月1日从HBO Max下架。

《世界大战》虽然讲的是外星人入侵，却也可以看作一则关于“9·11”袭击事件的寓言，而且这一层含义贯穿影片。故事从一个平凡的日子开始，突如其来的事件让一切变得可怕，从此再也无法回到原样。在影片中，外星人到来前，一股电磁脉冲使所有科技设备失效。随着故事推进，两者的相似之处愈发明显：人们发现外星人一直潜伏着，等待时机发动袭击，这呼应了人们对潜伏的恐怖分子的焦虑;片中甚至有角色直接问，眼前发生的一切是不是恐怖分子所为。影片还有许多令人联想到“9·11”的画面，包括能量武器袭击后灰烬覆盖一切的场景。
这些元素在2005年未必容易被接受。毕竟，“9·11”悲剧才过去四年，许多画面和感受仍历历在目。时间过去后，人们有了不同的视角。影片上映二十多年后，观众开始欣赏这个科幻故事如何融入人们经历过的恐惧与创伤，并最终讲述了一个关于坚韧的故事。
当然，影片大部分篇幅都在描绘人类求生时的混乱挣扎，但它也提醒人们，求生的意志可以成为强大的力量。如今，观众也开始欣赏影片的视觉效果。这并不意外：《世界大战》曾获得奥斯卡最佳视觉效果奖提名。外星三脚机器的设计，以及它们发出的声音，确实令人惊叹。
现在我们想问的是：《世界大战》上映多年后获得了新的认可，《Digger》将来也会如此吗?

items.title: 州诉讼指控 OpenAI 为了盈利而忽视自身的安全警告：“所有这些危害都是可以预见和避免的”
items.summary: Several US states have sued the company, alleging that ChatGPT is harming the public.

content.v: The attorney generals for eight US states announced today that they are suing OpenAI.

West Virginia, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana have all filed lawsuits alleging that the ChatGPT maker has deceived and endangered the public, particularly children, in the name of profit.

The complaints allege that ChatGPT has "coached" users to harm themselves and others, and—quoting the West Virginia filing specifically—state that "there is a growing body of research indicating that ChatGPT is also degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships."
Recent tales of "rogue" AI agents are also presented by as evidence of recklessness.

"All these harms were foreseeable and avoidable," reads the West Virginia complaint [ PDF ]. "[OpenAI CEO Sam Altman] himself has warned about the safety risks of AI since at least 2015. It is no secret that children use ChatGPT. And numerous OpenAI employees have left over safety concerns."

OpenAI acknowledged last year that its systems can "fall short" when responding to users in distress, but said that it has "a stack of layered safeguards" in place to help. The company also says on its website that it now uses "age prediction" to place some users in a teen-oriented ChatGPT experience with "additional safeguards," unless they verify that they are adults.

Separately from the state lawsuits, a class action lawsuit was filed in California on Tuesday on behalf of two children and "all other children similarly situated." That suit alleges that OpenAI has purposefully used ChatGPT to extract personal information from children, and has profited from that information by using it to train its models.

Again, Altman's own words form part of the basis for the suit: "People talk about the most personal shit in their lives to ChatGPT," Altman said on Theo Von's podcast last year. "People use it, young people, especially, use it as a therapist, a life coach."

The complaint asserts that, under California law, "it is illegal for an adult to secure, save, and monetize a child's 'most personal sh*t in their lives' and then claim the child somehow authorized that misappropriation for the adult's gain."
PC Gamer has reached out to OpenAI for comment on the lawsuits.

items.summary: The former Blizzard developer has moved on.

content.v: Despite some big changes happening with Overwatch lately, former game director Jeff Kaplan hasn't touched it since the year he left Blizzard. In fact, he actively avoids the game in every way he can, he told GameSpot in a recent interview.

Before Overwatch, Kaplan rose through the ranks on the World of Warcraft team, starting in QA and eventually becoming game director. He described his departure from the WoW team in 2008 as "a training moment" for when he would leave the Overwatch team, and Blizzard altogether, in 2021.

"I kind of went through a little bit of shock leaving WoW back in 2008," Kaplan says. "So, when I stepped away from Overwatch in April of 2021, I was kind of used to that moment of what it meant to give all of yourself, your heart, your soul–because it's not just a job, there's no one who can do this and have it just be a job–and then have this shocking moment where you realize it doesn't belong to you. It belongs to the team, belongs to the players, it belongs to Blizzard, but it doesn’t belong to you."

Kaplan says he "had a very almost clinical separation" with Overwatch after what he went through with WoW. As a result, he stopped playing it the moment he left and has actively avoided it ever since.

"After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read," he says. "I don't watch YouTube [videos]. I don't search for my name in Overwatch. I don't search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, 'Yeah, I'm not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I'm the Overwatch guy, but like, that's just not for me anymore.'"

In an interview from earlier this year , Kaplan said he fully expected to retire from Blizzard, but the company's former CFO broke him by threatening to lay off 1,000 people if Overwatch didn't meet certain financial goals. Kaplan called that meeting "the biggest fuck you moment I've had in my career, it felt surreal to be in that condition."

Kaplan went quiet for several years before reappearing with a new studio and a new open world survival cowboy game called The Legend of California , which he's heading up alongside former Blizzard developer Tim Ford. He says the new game is an opportunity to explore something more personal to him for the first time. "I didn't leave Blizzard to try to make a Blizzard game. I left Blizzard to make a Tim and Jeff game."

items.title: 我想喜欢新的恶魔城，但感觉有点不对劲
items.summary: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has the right pieces for a grand revival, but it hasn't quite nailed the assembly

content.v: I got off to a bit of an awkward start with Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when it first booted to a black screen. A few minutes of troubleshooting later, I deduced that the game wouldn't display on a monitor with its refresh rate set higher than 120 Hz. Easily solved, but I kept thinking of that quirk when I selected the in-game 120 fps cap and then watched the game jarringly lurch down to a lower framerate every time I hit a cutscene.

Maybe these technical quirks were treats for reviewers that have been smoothed over in time for launch. They haven't stopped me from having a lot of fun with the eight or so hours I've played Belmont's Curse—I think I'm closing in on the halfway point, and it keeps getting better as it goes. But it's not quite the slam dunk I expected from the first new Castlevania in decades, with such a talented studio behind it.

Belmont's Curse has a bit of a juice problem. You've probably heard (or said) "it's got the juice" so many times in recent years that the expression has more or less just become shorthand for I think this is really good . As originally coined by some very smart game designers , though, it means something a bit more specific: the sort of polish that "feels alive and responds to everything you do—tons of cascading action and response for minimal user input." There are some quintessential ways to add juiciness to an action game: screen shake, hitstop (the brief pause for impact when your attacks land), enemy reactions, flashy particles and other effects. Most important are how your character feels when they move or jump or dodge.

Juicy doesn't have to mean fast , necessarily. But Dead Cells, which Belmont's Curse developer Evil Empire spent much of the last decade working on, is one of the fastest and juiciest action games ever made. Hollow Knight's fast nail swipes and precise dodges are also extremely juicy, which is one reason it has so resoundingly become the metroidvania others are now measured against .
Belmont's Curse is somehow intermittently, confusingly juiced and… dry? Soured? There are ways in which it just feels off that are still bugging me hours into the game.

There's a lengthy wind-up on Rose Belmont's whip, which you use to swing all around France and Dracula's castle, that becomes a frustration during spike-filled platforming challenges that require perfect timing on a swing. Even when I get the timing right, I often miss a grapple point because I'm holding the analog stick in the direction I want to move rather than pointing it at the spot I need to hook onto.

The first dodge Belmont's Curse teaches you is a forward slide, but it has so few invincibility frames on it—if any at all—that it's gotten me killed in more boss fights than it has saved me. Maybe I should've learned by now not to use it, but it's just one of a dozen small things that I find fiddly or confusing in this game that I thought Evil Empire would absolutely have on lock.

Another one: Some tedious platforming challenges require phasing through specific walls and floors using a skill that, by default, is bound to the left trigger on a controller—which is fine until you have to pump it with a tiny margin for error. Phase through a wall (hold), then wall jump from it (release), then phase through another wall (hold), then land on one above a pit of spikes (release). Why bind that action to the analog input with the longest travel time on the controller?
Rose can use the whip to pull herself towards enemies and deliver a smashing blow, but the timing on that attack feels set too early.
Popping a healing flask requires holding a button down just long enough that I often think I've healed in the heat of battle until oops, surprise, dead.

And I know this is a budget limitation, but Belmont's Curse is clearly so inspired by the Netflix Castlevania series—it even includes a couple of the same voice actors—that some of the early cutscenes, which are disappointing panning shots of static artwork, really cry out for a more lavish presentation. They deserved a proper animated treatment that Konami apparently didn't shell out for.

Belmont's Curse doesn't make a great first impression, but once I reached Dracula's Castle after a few hours in Paris it started kicking things up a notch, with clever platforming gimmicks I've never run into before and clues pointing in the direction of each of Dracula's minions. It's a little bit more puzzley and thinky than many older Castlevanias, and I could see this being my favorite version of the castle to pick apart by the time I'm through with it.

And it's not totally juiceless! There's great, punchy hitstop when your attacks connect; the animation work is slick; the presentation of the tarot cards, which double as special weapons and guides to each boss you need to defeat, is gorgeous. I love flicking through them in my inventory.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LCujgfYPGWyYH6AJxDCK4m-1920-80.jpg

Were Evil Empire maybe trying so hard to ensure Belmont's Curse didn't feel like Dead Cells that it ended up with controls that didn't quite gel? It's a hard problem to articulate, but there's a little slack in this whip holding it back from being the return to Castlevania I want to wholeheartedly love.

items.title: 米克·戈登 (Mick Gordon) 讲述他如何帮助《战锤 40,000：爆弹枪 2》的高潮 Boss 战斗变得“宏大而夸张”
items.summary: Mick Gordon On How He Helped to Make Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2’s Climactic Boss Fight “Big and Bombastic”

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/05/19/boltgun-dlc-blogroll-1747685562957.jpg

If you were making a sequel to Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun and wanted to inject a bit of extra boom into the boomer shooter, then you probably wouldn’t look any further than Mick Gordon. The legendary Aussie composer has been soundtracking videogames for about two decades, but it was his face-melting work on 2016’s Doom and 2020’s Doom Eternal that really established his monster guitar riffs as the perfect way to fire up fans of first-person shooters. It seemed a no-brainer, then, that developer Auroch Digital would enlist Gordon to add his signature heavy touch to the climactic boss fight at the end of Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2. Ahead of the game’s release this week, IGN caught up with Gordon to get an insight into how his curtain-dropping contribution to the shooter sequel’s soundtrack came about.
IGN: How did you come to be involved with Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2? Were you familiar with the first game?

Mick Gordon: Yeah, definitely. So, I sent the team an email after the first Boltgun, and I said, “Hey, this game is really cool. There are a lot of boomer shooters out at the moment, but I think what you guys have done with it feels really good. It feels really fun to play. And you've obviously combined this pixelated, sprite-based, first-person shooter boomer shooter thing with the Warhammer 40K universe in what seems to be the most obvious idea that nobody else had ever thought of. Really, really great job.”

So, I had a bit of a relationship with them from that moment. And when they were doing the sequel, they shot me an email. They're like, "You know what? We've got this giant boss battle at the end, and it's on a scale that did not appear in the first game, and we want to have some music for it that kind of matches that scale, something that's really big and bombastic and silly. Would you like to do it?"

And of course, I was like, "Yeah, I'd absolutely love to." I've always wanted to, but I've never been involved in the Warhammer universe. I've always wanted to stray into that territory, but I've never [been] given an opportunity to until this one came along. So, there's the first-person shooter aspect, there's the Doom-inspired first-person shooter aspect, there's the pixelated aspect, there's this giant evil-looking demonic battle boss battle thing, and then there's the Warhammer thing. So, I mean, how would you not say yes to that? It's like a match made in heaven, really, isn't it?

IGN: When something like this kind of falls in your lap, do you start completely from scratch or do you have a folder on your MacBook that's labelled "Sick First-Person Shooter Riffs" and you just kind of scoop some of those out and start sculpting with them?

Gordon: No, definitely not. My job on every single project is to try to come up with a unique voice that suits that project and that project only. I like to think about these things as something that I come up with exists in a sphere in the universe, and that sphere belongs to that thing and that project, and that is unique in that space. When I'm coming up with something else, I can't push that sphere into the space that that other sphere exists in. Do you know what I mean? I have to come up with something that takes up its own space.

Now, of course, people will say, "Well, we've listened to your music. It sounds like you did this, sounds like you did this, you did this." I know you can never completely divorce yourself from your own tastes and input. So, I understand that. But my goal is to try and work with the team to come up with something unique that fits the music's purpose for that specific project alone. So, I don't just have like a bunch of [pre-existing] riffs or ideas that I would put into this game, and this game, and this game. That's not my job. My job is to sit with the team and try to find what makes their thing unique and really just explode that out [in an] extreme sort of way musically.
IGN: As part of your process for creating your track, ‘Ascent of the Arkifane’, did you actually play the boss battle itself?

Gordon: It can be difficult because often games aren't fun to play until they are finished and ready to release. You know what I mean? And often because of the rapid development on these games, there are builds being done several times a day. So, it can be very difficult for a team to send me a stable build to actually work with.

Instead, what they do is send me capture footage that the QA department puts together for me. And the QA people, it's their sole job to play the game all day. So, they are really good at it, and they're really good at making it look like it's how it's going to be. And that's perfect. That's all I need. They will send me that. They will send me screenshots. They will send me concept art. I will have conversations with the developers and things. But I love videos. Videos are the best.

Why I love the videos is I take the video when I get it in my studio, and I put the video on my television, and I sit on my couch, and I have a controller in my hands that is not even plugged in, right? It's just there, and I sit back on my couch and I start imagining myself as a player playing the game for the first time. The reason I'm doing this is I'm trying to find the most perfect tempo for what the music should be to match what I'm seeing. Then I have a little metronome app on my phone which is sitting on my thigh, and I will literally tap metronome tempos and write them in a notebook and say, "This level needs to be 99 beats per minute. This level needs to be 138. This one needs to be 216 beats per minute." And the whole reason I'm doing that is to try and find a tempo that fits with the natural pace of the gameplay itself.

I have to do that because if the music I make is too fast, it becomes overwhelming and annoying to the player. At that point, players go into the options menu and they turn the music down or off. And if they're doing that, I have completely failed. Not just at my job, but at life in general. If my music is too slow, that can result in reviewers saying, "This game feels sluggish. This game feels slow. The game itself didn't quite feel exciting." You know what I mean? That even if the game is tight, even if the game feels really good, the mechanics are there, everything is really nice and polished, if the music is too slow, the whole experience can feel really sluggish, you know?

So, my job is to just find the right tempo. Once I've got the tempo, then everything can get built from that point there. I set everything in my studio up to that tempo, and then I start building ideas out to match the game itself.

IGN: Once the developers of Boltgun 2 have given you artwork and gameplay videos, do you just lock yourself in your studio and produce the track on your own? Was there much back and forth with the development team?

Gordon: It's definitely a back and forth thing. I mean, you've got to understand when I start working on a project, there's nothing. Nothing exists. It's a complete blank canvas, you know? I don't even have a sharpened pencil at that point. It's nothing. And I get nothing for free. Like nothing. Nobody comes along and says, "Make this in D minor at 90 beats per minute" or whatever. Nothing. Nothing at all.

content.v: More radical changes beyond just giving the characters necks are coming to Garry's Mod successor s&box . Facepunch Studios' game creation platform's launch in April was met with a swarm of negative reviews, complaints of AI slop filling its user-generated game collection, and swiftly plummeting user numbers.

Now creator Garry Newman is reversing course on some of his decisions, such as pivoting to a 'greenlight type system' for user-generated games and announcing that the platform is going free to play much earlier than expected.

"Our focus has been on the engine and the development experience. That’s what we love, that’s what turns us on—but we’re not selling an engine, we’re selling a game," Newman wrote this week. "So we need to do much much better on the game, we need to shift our focus to what players are experiencing, not developers."

That focus, Newman said, will be on improving the sandbox mode for players by adding more NPCs, vehicles, and customization. "I’ve let everyone down that was expecting that. I accept that, and I’m sorry—we are going to do better," he said.
Another issue Newman addressed is making it easier for players to find quality games amidst the, and I quote, "ton of shit games" Facepunch has allowed creators to upload to s&box.
"The player is overwhelmed by choice," he said. "They choose a game, it takes a while to download, and it’s immediately shit. How many times will they try games until they find one they like?
"My idea of a Netflix for games doesn’t work. It’s not feasible. It’s not how people discover games. You can’t land people on a menu of 60 games and say, 'have fun'."

Game makers who want to participate in the Play Fund pool will now have to apply to the program, instead of the money automatically going to the games with the most maps and players. "Our new policy isn't set in stone, but generally we want to discourage clickers, idler, slop and UI based games," Newman said. "We want to set the bar a bit higher than it has been set previously. We've removed a bunch of games and maps from the system that we feel don't reach this new bar."

s&box is also going free-to-play before the end of 2026: "Everyone who has paid for the game will automatically get a bunch of exclusive steam inventory items (extra if you bought it at $20 vs $10) that I hope will justify the purchase price," Newman said.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WPEN28ofngL6izMFRFp6GV-1920-80.png

And finally, the sausage character model known as "The Citizen" or "Terry" (seen at the top of this page) has been retired in favor of generic human characters. "The model still exists in the game and so games that use it will keep using it, but it's no longer visible in the menu or the avatar editor."

Will those changes be enough to save s&box? Hard to say, but more curation by humans to keep out slop and less simply hoping that " slop will just fall to the bottom ," as Newman told me back in April, certainly seems like a wise adjustment. s&box definitely needs something : When Morgan played it back at launch, it felt like it contained very little of the spirit of the original G-Mod . Hopefully, these changes will help.

items.title: 传奇作曲家 Frank Klepacki 表示 RTS 类型并未消亡，但他希望看到开发者在其上发挥更多创意
items.summary: Klepacki shared his thoughts on the state of the real-time strategy genre in the latest issue of Edge.

others.title: GTA 6 Reviews: When They Could Be Released

content.v: Frank Klepacki has composed a lot of great game music over the years—in fact, he's responsible for the soundtrack in Eye of the Beholder 2, one of the best dungeon crawlers of all time . At heart, though, Klepacki is a real-time strategy guy—and he takes real issue with claims that the genre is dead.

There's no question that RTS is diminished, at least compared to its glory days. Back in the 1990s, games like Command & Conquer, Warcraft, and Dune 2 ( especially Dune 2, I'd say) dominated the scene. But all that remains of any of them these days is the seemingly unkillable World of Warcraft—and how many players even know that Blizzard's one true behemoth is an RTS spinoff?

Speaking in the latest issue of Edge, however, Klepacki said he thinks the genre still has lots of life in it. "There was all of this doom-and-gloom talk about ten years ago, saying, 'Oh, we think RTS is dead now—why are you still trying to work on games that are in a genre that’s going away?’" Klepacki said. "Obviously, if there are games coming out, [the genre is] not going away. It’s just that other types of games have taken the forefront of attention. Everything runs in cycles, you know? That’s how it always is."

That's true: RPGs have ebbed and flowed over the decades, and flight sims were huge until they weren't, and then they were again. But Klepacki also pointed the finger at a hollowing-out of the industry and growing aversion to risk, particularly among big-budget developers: "I would love to see more unique ideas that are allowed to be triple-A titles. A lot of indie titles are taking those creative chances, but a lot of the middle ground has gone."

Real-time strategy DNA has persisted in the MOBA genre, but traditional RTS games are enjoying a bit of a boom too. More than 20 years after Frozen Throne, Blizzard dropped a new campaign for Warcraft 3 in September, a Game of Thrones RTS is in the pipe, and Company of Heroes and Ruse are back; Age of Empires and Age of Mythology are still rumbling along, Tempest Rising delivers a very C&C-like experience, and while the new StarCraft game revealed at BlizzCon is a shooter, Blizzard is still dicking around with StarCraft 2 , too.
The days of building them around ensemble Hollywood casts may be over (at least for now), but the RTS itself? Be happy, Frank: it's definitely alive and kicking.

items.title: GTA 6 Was Originally Meant to Release Much Sooner Than We Realized
items.summary: Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, mean

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/gta-6-soundtrack-1789662158949.jpg
Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized.

As told in a new article from Bloomberg , Rockstar Games initially planned to develop Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 at the same time, but that quickly became infeasible. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recognized that the ambition behind Red Dead Redemption 2 meant they would need to treat it as an all-hands-on-deck situation, which also meant putting GTA 6 on the back burner. However, GTA 6 would benefit from this, as Nelson noted to Bloomberg that everything they built for Red Dead would "pay off" in GTA 6.

That appears to be true, as GTA 6 uses a lot of ideas and systems from Red Dead Redemption 2, including its NPC interaction system. It seems unlikely that GTA 6 would be what it is today if it had stayed the course and been developed in tandem with the western sequel. Unfortunately for fans, it means the game took much longer to make. Had it been developed simultaneously, it seems likely that Rockstar would've been able to release GTA 6 in the early 2020s.

Of course, the first release window that Rockstar ever actually publicly provided for GTA 6 was 2025. The game was delayed a couple of times, much to the bewilderment of Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive. Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe noted that she had to call Zelnick just months after announcing the game's first delay to inform him that they would need more time.

“I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” recalled Kolbe to Bloomberg. “But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great.”

Bloomberg's report dispels rumors that GTA 6 has been in active development since shortly after GTA 5 was released in 2013, but that doesn't mean Rockstar only began working on it after Red Dead 2's launch. Various teams and leadership within Rockstar have been researching and planning GTA 6 since as early as 2014. Rockstar has spoken at length in recent interviews about taking staff to Florida to research and dream up ideas for GTA 6 during the mid to late 2010s.

Bloomberg noted that the team didn't have a "skeleton" for GTA 6's story until the end of 2019, a year after Red Dead 2's release. Even then, it took a while before the team was able to fully wrap its head around what the game would be. Rockstar has vowed to not take nearly as long on its next game , thanks to the fact it seems to have fewer obstacles going forward.

Rockstar doubled in size during GTA 6's development, encountered multiple leaks, had a loss in productivity during the pandemic, and much more. The studio also made major changes to how it operates and expects that will set it up for success moving forward. What is Rockstar's next game? We don't know. Some may expect Red Dead 3, but other fans are hoping that Rockstar will break the cycle of alternating between Red Dead and GTA in favor of something new or reviving a different IP. Whatever the case is, don't expect it to take another eight years.

items.summary: Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming

content.v: Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years. Its biggest hurdle is still multiplayer games and their anti-cheat systems, but Epic Games is committed to bringing one of the biggest around to the operating system soon.

Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) , its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (itself included) opted not to use it and instead omit Linux support entirely because of its inability to be as protective as its Windows version.

A native rebuild of EAC, that doesn't require translation layers such as Proton, would help Epic bring the software up to par with Windows, at which point it would be comfortable finally releasing a native Linux version of Fortnite. In a blog post, Epic says that once it has reached this stage, it will make this available to other developers, too.

"We are also planning to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, where we’ll test it in a live environment and refine it based on what we learn. Once we’ve validated EAC v2’s effectiveness, we’ll make it available to more game developers so they can bring their multiplayer games to Linux players too."

Epic hasn't shared a timeline for when it expects Fortnite on Linux, but does say that its pilot program will be available through its new Epic Game Store launcher . Announced at the same time, Epic has decided to follow through with its commitment to AI-developed software earlier this week, with the new launcher labelled as "vibe coded" because "programming is hard". This version is still in preview and lacks all of the features currently on the main version of the store launcher, but Epic says that it is already seeing some speed improvements (even if they're just a few seconds here or there).

That might be too steep a price to pay depending on your appetite for linking your credit card details to an app that is being iterated on without much (or any) human intervention. And it's already led to some strange bugs that certainly would've been caught without being rushed into the hands of users.

items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going fo

content.v: Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going forward--possibly in a big way--and that's no surprise given Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to changes to the exclusivity strategy in the future .

At the same time, a survey like this is not necessarily indicative of anything beyond Microsoft conducting research. After all, there is an entire team at Xbox called Xbox Research that ... researches all manner of things, and the results of that research doesn't always lead to changes in the marketplace.
Windows Central reports that a new survey was issued to some Xbox Insiders this week, and the site confirmed the survey to be real.
The survey asks how members might feel about the totally nuclear option of making all Xbox-developed games except Call of Duty exclusive to Xbox on console.
"Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the survey asks.

It goes on: "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC with this announcement."
The survey asks respondents to say in this scenario, where they would be most likely to play any of the exclusive content. The choices are:
Another page of the survey specifically asks about Fallout, polling users about how they would feel if future Fallout games would be console-exclusive to Xbox, and with nothing changing at all on PC.
Windows Central reported that the survey also asked these same questions about The Elder Scrolls, Doom, Physint, Diablo, and Minecraft.
In a memo to staff, Sharma and Xbox boss Matt Booty said they will “re-evaluate” the approach to exclusivity , which could mean a lot of things. Surveying fans is likely connected to this endeavor.

Fans have called on Microsoft to return to exclusive games, but it remains to be seen if that will happen. Sharma and Booty also said they will consider changing things up in regards to “windowing,” which followed on from a report that said some other games beyond Call of Duty titles could be kept out of Game Pass at launch and for a period of time, similar to how movies are only available in theaters at first before coming to digital and streaming.

The so-called nuclear option of making all non-Call of Duty first-party games exclusive to Xbox on console would indeed be a bonafide return to exclusivity, but it also seems quite unlikely given how much money Microsoft could miss out on. At the same time, Sharma has pledged to fans that that Xbox needs exclusives to return to growth as part of the big Xbox "reset."

A survey like this offers an inherently hypothetical scenario, and it could simply be part of Microsoft's fact-finding mission to get a pulse of the fanbase. It would be an entirely different thing for Microsoft to commit to exclusives in this way and invest meaningfully to do so.
Sharma's other efforts so far as the new Xbox CEO have included mass layoffs, studio closures, and game cancellations. She has also said Microsoft's big bet on Game Pass did not work .

items.title: GTA 6 泄密者用“死人开关”威胁 Take-Two
items.summary: Cyberleek promises not to reveal the ending of GTA 6, as long as Take-Two leaves them alone.

content.v: It's a classic move: A villain, or sometimes a hero, inserts himself into a seemingly inescapable situation. Danger everywhere—no way out! But just as the good guys (or bad guys) are about to pounce, he holds up the pin he's pulled from the grenade under his coat, forcing everyone to back off! Escape is at hand!

That seems to be the strategy now adopted by notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek, and by "seems to be," I mean they stated it outright. In a message posted to their now-defunct website but preserved by GTA VI News on X , Cyberleek committed to not releasing anything more about GTA 6—including its ending, which at this point remains unknown—as long as Take-Two lets everything slide.

"CL has the ending. It was considered," the message states. "It would punish Take-Two greatly—but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy—why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough.

"The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leek—clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. The dead man's switch is active—story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/tq5sm4PPdFDjLzdxf2ody7-1920-80.jpg

A dead man's switch, generally speaking, is a switch built to be triggered if its operator is incapacitated. Miles Dyson, for instance, blew up Cyberdyne Systems with an improvised dead man's switch in Terminator 2 (not that it did much good) and Roger Murtaugh did the literal grenade-pin thing in Lethal Weapon while trying to save his daughter from Shadow Company goons. There are variants—in Point Break, for instance, Rosie was ordered to kill Johnny Utah's girlfriend if Bodhi didn't check in by 3, to ensure Johnny's participation in a bank robbery.
My own personal favorite dead man's switch comes from Hawk the Slayer:
That particular variation on the theme notwithstanding, dead man's switches are meant as last-ditch failsafes: If something bad happens to me, something much worse will happen to you .

It makes me wonder if Cyberleek's sudden withdrawal and proposed détente with Take-Two means that they're starting to feel the heat. Take-Two takes this sort of thing seriously as a matter of course, and you can bet it's going to go extra-hardass on anyone who messes with its biggest game ever, which GTA 6 unquestionably is. I have no doubt that life for Cyberleek will become very unpleasant, very quickly, if and when they're ever caught.

The problem Cyberleek faces, of course, is that their leverage—assuming it's real in the first place—has a very short shelf life. In six weeks at most, the GTA 6 ending will be out there, at which point there will be no shot left to shoot.

At best, then, this threat grants Cyberleek an extra month to find a deeper hole to hide in. And even that is wildly optimistic: Take-Two might be operating quietly, but I have no doubt that it's also operating furiously, and that there's not much of a mood to play 'I won't if you won't' games.

Cyberleek also defended their cryptocurrency ask, saying it "was always a donation, never an investment," and denying that a rugpull happened; they also said they wouldn't release the full build of GTA 6, with "full story mode, played to the end," because their memecoin market cap didn't hit $30 million .

items.summary: The biggest complaint about the pre-order bonus game is getting resolved with a happy ending.

content.v: Ace Combat 8 rocks. PC Gamer's reviewer scored it a 92% , and I've been savoring the campaign, because I know it could be years until we get another bombastic flight sim melodrama of its kind. Although I do have another Ace Combat lined up to play after: Ace Combat Zero, which was included as a free pre-order bonus with AC8, and subsequently responsible for the majority of the new game's negative launch day reviews.

Not because Zero is bad—it's a series fan-favorite—but because Bandai Namco inexplicably bundled it into the AC8 launcher, meaning you can't download this 3.2GB port of a 2006 PS2 game without the 136 gigabytes of Wings of Theve. This decision was not well received .

But now there's a happy ending: in an update on the Steam page on Tuesday, Bandai Namco announced that Ace Combat Zero "will be made available as a standalone application on Steam." That doesn't mean it will be made available for purchase: Zero was a pre-order bonus, so only those who bought Ace Combat 8 ahead of launch will have it in their Steam libraries. No change there. You'll just be able to download and launch it independently if you already own it. It's currently going through "final quality assurance and compatibility testing" ahead of the split.

The biggest benefit from the change (aside from potentially freeing up 136GB of precious SSD space) is that Zero will now support Steam Cloud saves. Judging by the nearly 400 comments on the post in less than 24 hours, the news has gone over very well—though there are also quite a few requests for the standalone Zero to include achievements, which were part of the console release.
There's no date given for Zero's emancipation, but presumably it won't be too far off.

items.summary: The Electronic Software Association (ESA) has a serious bone to pick with retro handhelds that are packaged wi

content.v: The Electronic Software Association (ESA) has a serious bone to pick with retro handhelds that are packaged with tons of unlicensed pre-installed, calling these devices "superfakes" that should face some sort of suppression by the US government.

According to an October 6 filing with the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR)--which monitors marketplaces that are accused of engaging in or enabling piracy and counterfeiting--the ESA is urging the government to clamp down on what it calls "illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices." The ESA wants the USTR to add these emulation devices to the Notorious Markets List, the agency's annual report identifying which markets are participating in such behavior, thereby barring or slowing their profits.

"In the video game sector, illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices are the functional equivalent of superfakes," the ESA told the USTR. "They can look and feel like legitimate, mass-market consumer electronics: molded housings, color displays, polished user interfaces, retail packaging, product reviews, warranty-like representations, and listings on familiar e-commerce platforms. Yet their commercial appeal rests solely on a concealed memory card or internal drive loaded with hundreds, thousands, or even tens of thousands of unauthorized copies of copyright-protected games."

The ESA puts a specific spotlight on Anbernic , a console manufacturer that sells 3DS- and Game Boy-looking devices packed with thousands of games from systems like the NES and SNES to the PlayStation 1 and Sega Genesis. Though maybe the most prominent example, another one that comes to mind is rapper Soulja Boy's various console attempts .

The filing also targets digital marketplaces that it says distribute or sell modded accounts and pirated games such as Eldorado, FunPay, G2A, and Voices38. In short, the ESA is seeking some kind of restitution for the harm that "superfake" retro consoles pose to the gaming industry writ large.

"A single device can substitute for lawful purchases across multiple video game publishers and console generations, divert sales from authorized games, compilations, subscriptions, remasters, and licensed retro hardware," the ESA wrote. "Because the product is often delivered with an immediately usable catalogue of pirated games, it removes the technical friction that once separated mainstream consumers from video game piracy. Sellers commonly use the illicit library as a key selling point, and the commercial price often reflects this."

And then, off I went, sailing through the streets of Los Santos in my shiny car in the night (sometimes in the day) and whacking the eject key to hop out. A Gears of War: E-Day mod lets players fancast your own team of Gears, with options from everything from Halo spartans to Space Marines from Warhammer 40,000.

The Incursion mod streamlines what’s usually a multi-mod setup for this kind of thing. items.title: 回顾《守望先锋》的 10 年，兑现的承诺以及 Team 4 的未来
items.summary: "In order for people to play the game in the present, they need to have confidence in its future."

content.v: 10 years is a long time for anything, but for a live service game it's a milestone that very few are able to cross. Overwatch made it over the line earlier this year, and has since been able to do something of a victory lap because after all the highs and the lows, Overwatch is in the best place it's ever been .

"It doesn't feel like 10 years to me," game director Aaron Keller tells me. "Although, I could probably answer that question in a few ways. There's probably a year or two that might have felt like five or six years in the middle of this process, but there's always so much to be doing on the team and for the game." But Keller reiterates the good old adage "if you love what you do, you never work a day in your life.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xdcPtestjJHLDAJEgWhDeR-1920-80.jpg

"Our team is filled with people that are not just passionate about making games, they're passionate about Overwatch itself, our heroes and the world in which they reside. So when you get to go into the office and talk about that all day, the time can fly by pretty quickly."

Alec Dawson, associate game director, joined before the launch of Overwatch 2 but also feels as if these last four years have flown by "in a blink of an eye … It's wild that when we started the year, we had these silhouettes of heroes that we didn't even know what they were going to be, what they were going to look like, and now we do," Dawson adds. "Sometimes it just goes by much quicker than you think it's going to."

Overwatch has undergone many metamorphoses, some good, others not so good. We had the early golden years, then we had GOATS, then a plethora of some of the best game cinematics ever, then we had early Brigitte taking a literal hammer to the game's balance.

After something of a content drought, excitement was renewed with the announcement of Overwatch 2, and while this did offer a lot of good changes like more heroes, content, and focused team fights in 5v5, it failed to meet the requirements of a sequel , and that's without the disappointment surrounding PvE .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8tACEUQZmSoZq4PiuBwHVJ-1920-80.jpg

There was a time when I thought that was it for Overwatch, that PvE and Overwatch 2 would be all anyone would ever talk about. But I've never been happier to be proven wrong, because all these years later Overwatch is going from strength to strength experimenting with things like perks and Stadium, tweaking the user experience with map voting and hero bans, and changing to a new annual content release format.

"I don't think we could honestly say we knew it would go this far," Keller says. "I believe that there's always been something special about Overwatch. There's something special about the world. This optimistic, hopeful take on the future. I do think that there's something special about the gameplay—it's so crisp and clean—and there's moments you have in Overwatch that you just don't really get to have in other games."

I've said it before but the current success that Team 4 is seeing didn't just happen overnight . It's been a long road, one marked with deliberate decisions and remedies taken by its devs. The passion the devs have exhibited, the humility to admit when things aren't working, and keeping player's best interests at the forefront are why the game is in such a good state today.
What promises have Team 4 kept over the last 10 years?
Next up

Moving on from its tenth anniversary year, Overwatch has a new seasonal cadence which has not only worked to spark excitement, but as Keller sees it, has bolstered the "belief that Overwatch is really going in a good direction." There's a steady flow of quality-of-life changes to its UI as we saw last season with new heal, burn, and team indicators. Team 4 has given players more freedom when it comes to picking Drives, and the narrative story is back to being central to Overwatch's experience.

There's obviously going to be a steady flow of new content and characters, but Dawson has also confirmed that map reworks and tweaks will be "something we want to continue doing". Informed by map voting and community feedback the team will ensure that reworks "can stand on its own" not only fixing problems but gunning for a better overall experience: "I think our next rework does a pretty good job of that."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/NQfwNpKnFqE3StyLVtegAJ-1920-80.png

"We're really far into development on Season 1 for 2027," Keller reveals. "We're talking about what Season 1 is going to look like in 2028, and getting started on that. We want it to feel like not just one big moment but that the game is fresh for players and that we are getting players to look at it through new eyes again—we want to do it in a different way each year."

But while Team 4 gets stuck into planning content for the years to come, Dawson stresses that their overall mission will stay the same: "As much as the industry has changed, games have changed, genres, etc. Overwatch is still home for so many people. It's a really big responsibility that we take to heart of making sure that Overwatch can be a part of those people's lives as long as possible.

"To make sure they have the game and the heroes that they can relate to, make sure that they can play with their friends, and just keep having that place where they feel like, okay, this is where I want to be. This is where I want to spend my time. This is where I want to make memories. Hopefully, we can keep carrying that into the future as well."

items.title: 前《守望先锋》总监杰夫·卡普兰表示，他从来不想成为聚光灯下的焦点，但游戏需要一张面孔
items.summary: Being the face of a video game is a demanding role, as the people who step into these positions involved in th

content.v: Being the face of a video game is a demanding role, as the people who step into these positions involved in these roles often find themselves on the receiving end of a lot of toxicity. Former Overwatch game director Jeff Kaplan knows this all too well, as he promoted the hero shooter for several years and regularly interacted with its fans--albeit at a "personal cost."

After leaving Blizzard Entertainment in 2021, Kaplan has been quietly working on The Legend of California , the in-development game at his new studio, Kintsugiyama. Reflecting on his time as the face of Overwatch, Kaplan spoke to GameSpot about how Overwatch needed someone to fill that role. For Kaplan, this was part of Overwatch's growth and continued existence, and he felt it was needed at the time.

"This is going to sound ridiculous, but I'm not someone who likes attention," Kaplan said of his time in the public-facing position. "I'm not much of an extrovert. I don't have a heavy social media presence. And so, a lot of me putting myself out there when I was at Blizzard was sort of to serve my game and my team--doing a job and a role."

Overwatch--and Blizzard as a whole--has had tremendous highs and lows over the years. During periods of content droughts or Hero changes, players would often target Kaplan and other developers on the game with verbal abuse and threats. There has never been a silver bullet to eliminate player toxicity, but Blizzard discovered that dropping a ton of content into Overwatch helped change player sentiment .
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OW-heroes.png?w=636

While his departure from Blizzard back in 2021 wasn't easy, Kaplan said that being freed of the responsibility of being associated with Overwatch and fading into the background turned out to be "pretty great" in the end.

"There were a lot of emotions mixed up in leaving Blizzard, but one of the things that was sort of much needed for me, on a personal level, was that withdrawal," Kaplan said. "To stop reading the subreddits, to not talk to anybody. It's not like I had a game that I needed to talk to anybody about, and I don't have the need to see my name in headlines or, you know, like, 'Let's Google and see where I'm being mentioned today.' That's just not me as a person. So, it was very soothing to my soul to sort of fade into the background and just put all of that aside for some time. It was pretty great, actually. It was very needed for me."

Kaplan went on to explain his thoughts on if studios even need a public face for their games, citing both Valve and Rockstar as companies that "do a great job of promoting their games" despite not having a designated speaker.

"There doesn't need to be [one]," Kaplan said. "But I think it was good for Overwatch to sort of let the players know, 'We're one of you, we're listening.' It showed a level of transparency and engagement, like, 'Hey, this thing is being made by real people.' Blizzard always runs the risk of kind of, 'Oh, it's just a nameless, faceless corporation' if we don't put ourselves out there.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jeff-kaplan-stop-complaining-about-games-you-wont-play-shut-v0-cn4TnuirbR-XdIZHUsXZfXWaEtggzJmlo7eT0qk_b08_662b5b.webp?w=636

"I think people like [current Overwatch director] Aaron [Keller] or myself, kind of [thought], 'Hey, we should really let these people know: We play the game too. We have opinions too.' That was sort of the strategy, but it comes at a cost to you personally. I know a lot of extroverts who love it and are like, 'I just did press for eight hours, and I feel energized!' And I'm like, 'Oh my god, I need to hide under a rock for seven days because I did one interview.'"

Currently, Kaplan and the rest of the team at Kintsugiyama are working on The Legend of California, a multiplayer survival-action game set in the wild west. The title doesn't have a release date yet, but if you're interested in taking part in an upcoming playtest for the open-world shooter, you can check out its Steam page and request access.

items.title: Jeff Kaplan Says Separation From Overwatch Was “Clinical”: ” I Never Go Back”
items.summary: Jeff Kaplan, Overwatch's former director, said he's not played the game he was the public face of since April

content.v: Jeff Kaplan, Overwatch's former director, said he's not played the game he was the public face of since April 2021, when he left developer Blizzard after nearly 20 years to go indie. He called his relationship with Blizzard's shooter one of "clinical separation."
Kaplan revealed this to GameSpot in an interview that dove into his history with Blizzard and the creation of his new game, The Legend of California .

When asked if he had continued to play Overwatch or kept tabs on it in the wake of it dropping the "2" from its name and its addition of 10 new heroes over the course of the year, Kaplan said he hadn't. He said he's essentially cut all ties with the game he used to direct.
"With Overwatch, I had a very almost clinical separation, knowing how the WoW thing had gone," Kaplan said. "I've literally not played the game since April 2021."

He continued: "I don't, for my own psyche, I don't read the subreddits. After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read. I don't watch YouTube [videos]. I don't search for my name in Overwatch. I don't search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, 'Yeah, I'm not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I'm the Overwatch guy, but like, that's just not for me anymore.'"

It was a lesson Kaplan learned when he left the World of Warcraft team in 2008 after working on Blizzard's MMORPG for six years. He said it was more painful to step away from WoW than it was for Overwatch.

"Oddly, leaving WoW was a training moment for me," he said. "When I left WoW to work on Titan [the game that would eventually become Overwatch], it was, I think, November or December of 2008. And WoW was who I was at that point. I worked every minute--every waking minute--on WoW. If I wasn't working on WoW, I was playing WoW. And every time I played WoW, I had this notepad next to the desk that I'd be filling out to walk in the next morning and go, 'These are all the things we need to change.'
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/4669062-wow.webp?w=636
"It was kind of shocking in a very negative emotional way to step away from WoW, because it was such a part of who I was and how I identified. It was who I was as a game developer."

As a result, when it came time to leave Overwatch and Blizzard behind, Kaplan said he was "used to that moment" of having given everything to a game, and the need to establish a "healthy separation" between him and his former work.

"I was kind of used to that moment of what it meant to give all of yourself, your heart, your soul--because it's not just a job, there's no one who can do this and have it just be a job--and then have this shocking moment where you realize it doesn't belong to you. It belongs to the team, belongs to the players, it belongs to Blizzard, but it doesn't belong to you," Kaplan said.
Kaplan said he was trying to avoid becoming Uncle Rico from the film Napoleon Dynamite, an old man reliving his glory days of playing football by watching tapes of his games.

"I don't want to be Uncle Rico," Kaplan said. "Overwatch happened. I was a part of it. There's a group there now and Overwatch is now about them. Both the players and the developers, that's their Overwatch now. They're making it, they own it, they play it. I'm onto this new thing, and that's where I'm at in my life."

items.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced was a big hit, and now it's time for big layoffs at the studio that made it
items.summary: Ubisoft has also decided to close Trials studio Ubisoft Redlynx entirely.

content.v: Three months after the very successful launch of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced , a game that sold two million copies in a single day ( three million copies in a week!) and surpassed "annual expectations" in just two weeks, Ubisoft has laid off 70 people from developer Ubisoft Singapore. In a statement provided to PC Gamer, the publisher also said it plans to close the Ubisoft Redlynx studio outright.

This would be reason number two on our list of 25 foolproof ways to get laid off in the videogame industry: Make a game that sells so well, it blows away all expectations and makes even more money than anyone dared hope.
Of course, we've already seen this in play with Black Flag Resynced—Ubisoft Barcelona, a support studio on the game, had nearly a third of its number cut shortly after it launched.

The Ubisoft Barcelona layoffs might seem particularly egregious, coming so soon after it produced a much-needed win for a publisher that's spent the past few years taking big Ls , but it's not the only bad news.

A year after announcing a " restructuring proposal " for Ubisoft Redlynx aimed at reducing costs and ensuring "a stronger prioritization and efficiency across the company’s worldwide studio network," Ubisoft has now decided to close the studio outright.

Founded in 2000 and acquired by Ubisoft in 2011, Redlynx is best known for the Trials motorcycle racing games, the last of which— Trials Rising —came out in 2019. Since then, the studio supported the development of Star Wars Outlaws and released the mobile game Gwen's Getaway; a VGC report says Ubisoft decided to close Redlynx because it's not currently working on anything else, and downsizing wouldn't make it sustainable anyway.
Ubisoft acknowledged "the contributions" of the employees being put out of work in its statement, and said it will conduct the process "with care and respect."

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/13/diablo-immortal-spawn-figure-1791922260266.jpg
IGN Fan Fest is kicking off today, and as part of the celebration, we’re showing off a Spawn Warlock action figure that commemorates the anti-hero’s special collaboration with Diablo Immortal.

As revealed at Blizzcon 2026 , Diablo Immortal is currently in the midst of a crossover event with Spawn, which runs from September 29 to November 1. This month-long extravaganza features a slew of new Spawn-themed challenges, abilities, and of course, a Spawn-themed cosmetic set.

The Warlock class version of this skin set is coming to the real world in the form of a 7-inch deluxe action figure from McFarlane Toys. Designed with ultra articulation and up to 22 moving parts, this figure has a full range for making cool poses. It includes a wired fabric cape, the Hellspawn Subjugator Sacrificial Blade, Demon Skull, and four alternate hands.
This figure also comes with an Elite Points card, which can be redeemed on the McFarlane Rewards website to snag rewards and one-of-a-kind prototypes, as well as a collectible art card.

Perhaps the most standout feature of this figure is Spawn’s wired cape, which manages to bring McFarlane’s signature, larger-than-life style to reality. The devil is in the details here (no pun intended), with every bit of in-game armor represented in the figure’s model.
Pre-orders are available now at McFarlane Toys’ official website and select retailers for $49.99. The figure is set to release in March 2027.

Diablo is having a big moment right now; on top of Immortal’s Spawn collaboration, Diablo V was announced at this year’s Blizzcon, which is scheduled for release in 2029. An animated show is also in the works at Netflix, though not much is known about the project at present.

We got the chance to interview the developers behind Diablo V to talk about the game, who confirmed that development is already in full swing.
